materials: horizontal lap aluminum siding, 200 mm exposure: grey (about #A6ABAB) below the sills, off-white (about #DCDDD7) above, split by an aluminum strip

homes.notes: Box 4.88 x 18.70 m (16 x 61 ft) inside the 5.0 x 19.0 m Atlas footprint; floor 0.86 m above grade on the chassis, side walls to 3.04 m, bowed roof crown 3.26 m (Atlas height 3.5 m). From the photo: the single-wide type and proportions, grey and white horizontal siding, the low metal roof with rust, skirting to the ground, aluminum windows, the wooden steps with a railing. From the brief: door on the long side facing the stub, landing with steps and railing, window AC, gravel pad, propane cylinder, trash bins, folding chair, short clothesline. Interpreted (not in the photo or brief): the two-tone split at sill height, cross-seam spacing, the window layout (living room at the lane end, bedrooms at the north end), the back door and its stoop, roof jacks, the storm door, the second cylinder, the recycling cart, the power pedestal, hose and loose blocks. The lot is the strip beside the trailer only (neighbours stand 11.5 m east and west, so it is held to x = -5.7..5.7); the gravel pad meets the lane edge at y = -10.95 and opens toward the access stub on its west side.

homes.name: Delacroix house
homes.status: proposed (address and placement); design from the author's film still (reference/lori-house.webp), detail from reference/board-17.jpg and board-19.jpg
materials: warm red-brown brick in Flemish bond with darker burnt headers, light mortar
darker brick base with a limestone water table
dark natural slate hipped roof with lead hip and ridge caps, copper valleys
white painted dentil cornice, pediment, pilasters, portico and balustrade
black louvered shutters, 6-over-6 white sash windows, arched fanlights
limestone sills, jack-arch lintels and keystones; bluestone terrace and treads
lead-coated copper bay roof, aged copper downspouts
asphalt drive with Belgian-block (granite) edging, brick paver landing and terrace
homes.notes: Main block 18.0 x 11.5 m (x -9..9, y -5.75..5.75), first floor 0.60 m above grade, second floor 4.15 m, cornice soffit 7.2 m, 34 deg slate hip to a 11.9 m ridge; twin corbelled end chimneys to 13.55 m. The Atlas height (8.0 m) is too low for a 2.5-story Georgian house with the tall roof in the photo, so the ridge is about 48% higher. The pavilion projects 1.0 m; the portico, terrace and steps reach y = -10.5 (1.1 m beyond the footprint). Wings make the house about 30 m wide: the 1.5-story front-gabled left wing (x -15..-9) and the two-story hipped right wing (x 9..15). From the photo: brick, dark slate hip, tall corbelled chimney, white columned portico with balustraded balcony, pedimented pavilion with an arched fanlight rising into the pediment, black shutters, front-gabled left wing, the shed-roofed porch between the wing and the portico, lanterns, arched first-floor windows on the right, attic dormers, curving drive. Interpretations: the side, rear and roof plan (rear ell, dormers front and back, side entry, chimney positions), the box bay on the wing (after board-19), Flemish bond, the drive layout (a horseshoe with a planted island and a spur to a parking court at the right wing), gate piers, rear terrace and the three hardwoods. The lot GLB has no lawn; its drive meets the curb line exactly at two flared mouths. The lot owns its frontage: the brick gate piers stand 3.95 m behind the curb line (caps 3.58 m), so nothing walled or hedged sits in the 1.8-3.3 m sidewalk zone; only the drive and its granite edging run to the curb. The three hardwoods (white-oak habit, 16.5-18 m) are a trunk with root flares, scaffold limbs, branches and twigs carrying about 530 small soft leaf clumps each in a lobed crown shell, shaded by vertex colour (darker inside and underneath); no alpha cards.

The photo shows a long ridge with near-vertical roof ends, so the hip ends are pitched steeper (60 deg) than the front and back (38 deg). Wraparound porch 3.0 m deep on the front and both sides; the left return stops short of the side wing, the right return has brick steps at its back end toward the driveway. From the photo: massing, three dormers with sawn bargeboards and finials, scalloped fascia, turned posts with fan brackets, sawn balusters, balcony with flower boxes, double entry with sidelights and transom, lanterns, brick steps, slatted porch skirting, white picket fence with an X-braced gate, brick walk, rounded ornamental tree right of the walk, and the two moss-hung live oaks (both stand front left in the photo; the brief put one behind the house, the photo was followed). Interpreted (not visible in the photo): side and rear elevations, the hipped side wing, the rear kitchen ell and stoop, chimney positions on the rear slope, lattice under the house block (per the brief), shell driveway with concrete apron, mailbox, HVAC condensers, roll carts, porch rockers, swing and ferns.

Interpreted: side and rear elevations, rear doors, the exterior chimney, beds and props. No fence or hedge on the frontage.

No fence or hedge along the frontage (the lot owns its frontage; the walk and drive run to the curb line).

landmarks.name: Carnegie Library (1912)
landmarks.notes: Interpretation (no reference image): a small 1912 Beaux-Arts Carnegie library in buff brick on a raised ashlar base; a projecting pedimented entry pavilion with two columns in antis, bronze doors and a lunette over a flight of eight steps with lamp standards; tall arched windows with stone keystones; stone corner pilasters, entablature, a balustraded parapet and a low verdigris dome over the reading room. The site-specs method puts the front toward Fourth Street (heading 87.6) although the address is on Third Street.

landmarks.name: Chadwick's
landmarks.notes: Interpretation: a classic one-story diner filling the Atlas footprint: a full-width dining room across the front with a continuous band of big windows (stainless mullions, see-through glass), cream enamel and a red stripe, a rounded stainless roof edge, a glass entry vestibule and deep red canvas awnings; inside a checkerboard floor, booths along the windows, a counter with eleven stools, a back bar and lit pendants; a painted-block kitchen behind with rooftop units. The Atlas height (12 m) is far above a one-story diner; the model is 5.0 m. No sign or name on the building.

landmarks.name: Lindon County Courthouse
landmarks.notes: Interpretation (no reference image): a two-story neoclassical red-brick courthouse on a rusticated stone basement, stone quoins, belt course, keystone lintels and arched second-floor windows; a hexastyle giant-order portico with a pediment and oculus over a broad flight of granite steps; slate hip roof; a white cupola with four clock faces (no numerals), an octagonal colonnaded lantern and a verdigris copper dome. The site-specs method puts the front toward Jefferson Street (heading 178.1), not Second Street (its address); the Atlas building is 40.01 x 60.03 m with the long side running back from the street.

landmarks.name: the pier and the pier bar
landmarks.notes: Origin = the platform center at map grade z = 0; the deck top is z = 1.2 (PIER_DECK_Y = WATER_Y + 1.9), pilings run to z = -4. The app draws pier 12 as a 3 m deck (175.1 m long); this model brings its own 16 x 20 m pier-head platform that starts exactly at the seaward end of that polyline (so the app deck and rails do not overlap it) and runs 20 m on along the last segment; the 10 x 14 m bar sits on it with 3 m of deck all round. Front (-Y) faces back up the pier toward Harbor Drive; the rail has a 3.6 m opening where the pier comes in. Atlas building 58 (a shop at the old pier-bar point) is the bar it replaces; hide it. distance_along_pier_m is the platform center measured from the land end, 10 m past the polyline end.

landmarks.name: water tower (FOUNDED 1625)
landmarks.notes: Classic six-leg elevated steel tank, pale blue-grey (#B2C1CB), 13 m tank on battered tubular legs with tie-rod X bracing, a balcony at the shell bottom, central riser and a caged ladder. Lettering is real geometry (DejaVu Sans Bold, navy), WESTPORT over FOUNDED 1625, on the front (toward Mariner Drive) and the back. Center is the QA-moved place point (qa.json move_places), which is also the center of Atlas building 57 (kind civic in the Atlas, not "tower"). Leg footings spread to a 16.4 m circle, a little beyond the 12 m Atlas square.

landmarks.name: Williams Funeral Home
landmarks.notes: Interpretation (no reference image): a two-story Greek Revival house in white-painted brick under a slate hip roof, with a full-height four-column portico and pediment, black shutters on 6-over-6 windows, lanterns, a small balcony over the entry, a one-story chapel wing on the left, a porte-cochere and garage on the right and a rear ell. No signs. Front faces Main Street; the building sits back from the curb as the Atlas footprint does.
